assignmentTitle: Analysis of an Automobile Suspension System

criteria.title: Observe the Suspension System
criteria.description: Understanding client brief, automobile motorcycle rear suspension system, and project scope.

criteria.title: Identify Suspension Components
criteria.description: Accurate labeling of frame, swingarm, pivot, spring, damper, mounts, linkage, axle, wheel, and tyre on EA-15.

criteria.title: Understand the Load Transmission Path
criteria.description: Tracing load flow from road impact through tyre, wheel, axle, swingarm, spring-damper unit, and upper mount to frame chassis.

criteria.title: Identify Component Functions
criteria.description: Explaining individual mechanical functions of swingarm, mounts, spring, damper, axle, and frame.

criteria.title: Spring and Damper
criteria.description: Contrasting elastic energy storage (spring) vs kinetic vibration dissipation (damper).

criteria.title: Suspension Movement
criteria.description: Analyzing mechanical bump compression and rebound expansion dynamics.

criteria.title: Suspension Performance
criteria.description: Evaluating trade-offs between ride comfort, spring stiffness, damping rate, and high-speed stability.

criteria.title: Practical Suspension Condition Analysis
criteria.description: Diagnosing suspension faults (uncontrolled bouncing, bottoming out, harshness) and identifying root causes.

criteria.title: Engineering Decision Making
criteria.description: Rendering system-level suspension tuning recommendations for dual-rider touring vs off-road riding.

criteria.title: System-Level Engineering Analysis
criteria.description: Synthesizing comprehensive system-level analysis report covering load path, spring-damper roles, fault diagnosis, and maintenance.
